goals.title: Dual-source search: local library plus YouTube
goals.description: Design frames 1f, 1g and 1h. One search field querying two sources at once: the indexed local music folders (instant, already available via LibraryIndex in ipod-gui.py) and YouTube via 'yt-dlp ytsearch --flat-playlist --dump-json'. Local results paint immediately; YouTube results arrive 1-3s later into a reserved three-row skeleton so the layout never jumps. Note that youtube_unavailable_reason() is too strict to gate search on its own, because metadata search works without a JavaScript runtime; only the media download 403s. Reuse yt_dlp_bin and yt_dlp_supports from lib.sh. Design all five failure states: no JS runtime, ffmpeg missing, rate-limited or offline, download failed mid-fetch, and no results from either source. Each must be stated inline in place of the section that cannot load, never as a toast.

goals.title: Search UI polish deferred from the redesign
goals.description:
Small things the phase-1 redesign left, all in ipod-gui.py. The library filter pills count collections but the heading and counts stay collection-shaped while the list mode shows tracks, which reads slightly off. The album detail's state, duration and action cluster sits hard against the right edge with a wide gap after the title column. The playlist rail and the shelf both render the same playlists with different tile sizes. None of these block anything; fold them into whichever phase touches those views next.

Done 2026-08-04. The library heading, its pill counts and what those pills filter now follow the mode: list mode reads Tracks over per-track counts, and filters the tracks themselves, so a synced track is no longer hidden by its album still counting as In library. LibraryIndex gained track_counts() for that, which counts() cannot answer.

The album page is held to TRACK_PAGE_WIDTH in an Adw.Clamp, header and table together. Unclamped it had been the worst case in the app: on a 1900px window the title ended at x=460 and the state, duration and action cluster sat at x=1680. The playlists detail took the same clamp, since its rows are the same rows and it stretches further still.

Playlist artwork is now three named sizes rather than four arbitrary ones: the shelf tile takes ALBUM_COVER so the two sections of the library page use one artwork size, and both rails take PLAYLIST_ROW_COVER so a playlist row looks the same in the sidebar and in the Playlists view. Shelf tiles were also ragged - each sized to its own name - and are now uniform, with the card inset left to the button's own padding so four playlists and the New tile still fit at the opening window size.

Two defects surfaced while looking at these views and were fixed with them: the Playlists rail took a share of every extra pixel of window, because the heading and every row expand and GTK propagates that up, so at 1900px a 240px list held half the view; and the playlist's spoken-name line wrapped at 34 characters however much room it had.

Verified by rendering each view offscreen at 1180 and 1900 and reading the result, since x11grab sees black under Wayland and a WidgetPaintable holds nothing when the compositor is not sending the window frames: forcing the layout with Gtk.Widget.allocate and snapshotting into a Cairo renderer makes the size a parameter of the shot rather than whatever the window manager gave.

goals.title: GStreamer preview playback and the live now-playing bar
goals.description: The now-playing bar exists in ipod-gui.py in its idle state only; its transport controls are insensitive. Wire it to GStreamer playbin3 with position polled on a 250ms GLib timeout, per design frame 1n, which specifies all four bar states: idle, fetching, playing a local file, and playing a previewed track. Playback is preview only, on the computer's speakers, and never touches the iPod. Add a gst_available predicate to lib.sh modelled on find_gui_python - a separate function, because extending find_gui_python would make the whole GUI unavailable when GStreamer is missing - and reach it from the GUI through the existing lib_function_succeeds bridge. Adding system dependencies is approved, so this needs no further sign-off. Note python3-gi-cairo is still NOT required: the storage meter uses a CSS gradient rather than Cairo drawing, deliberately, because a missing converter would make the bar silently render as nothing.

goals.title: Preview cache with promote-on-add
goals.description: Previewing a YouTube result downloads it first (about 4s) rather than streaming: yt-dlp -g URLs are short-lived and IP-bound, seeking over HTTP is unreliable, and streaming throws the work away so Add would fetch a second time. Downloads land in a prunable cache, not straight into the library, so previewing twenty songs does not silently add twenty files to the user's music folder. Adding a previewed track promotes it into ~/Music/youtube and out of the cache. This is what finally creates the third track state, STATE_PREVIEW, which ipod-gui.py already defines and renders everywhere (dimmed artwork, dashed marker) but nothing currently produces. Wire up the Preview cache card in Device and Settings, which is present but shows 0 B and has its Clear button disabled.

goals.title: YouTube thumbnails as album art
goals.description: Search results and previewed tracks need artwork. ipod-fetch.sh passes --no-embed-thumbnail explicitly, commented 'Cover art is pure waste on a 2GB device with no screen' - still true for the device, but the desktop grid needs it. Either fetch thumbnails separately into the existing art cache or revisit that flag for previewed tracks only. Load them as GdkTexture through the existing make_cover helper, which already handles a missing-art fallback to a generated striped placeholder.

goals.title: Add GStreamer to install.sh as an optional system dependency
goals.description: Follow the existing capability-probe pattern in install.sh: probe for the capability rather than the package name, print an 'info' line when present, and append apt names to the 'needed' array when absent. GStreamer belongs in 'needed' like ffmpeg, not in the js_runtime exception - that exception exists because Ubuntu ships nodejs 18 below yt-dlp's floor of 22, and GStreamer has no equivalent version hazard. Add a matching line to the Verifying section. PyGObject stays out of the venv for the documented reason, so anything GStreamer-Python is a system dependency too.

goals.title: Split ipod-gui.py into a package and modernise the test harness
goals.description: ipod-gui.py is now a very large single module and wants to be a package. It was deliberately left as one file: the three smoke tests load it via spec_from_file_location with no package context and no sys.modules entry, and they patch module globals late (ipod_gui.find_ipods, ipod_gui.YOUTUBE_LIBRARY). A naive split silently breaks that patching - 'from .detect import find_ipods' rebinds the name and the detection test would pass against unpatched code, which is worse than failing. Do the split together with a test-harness rewrite. Also extend the CI Python gate, currently only 'py_compile ipod-gui.py tests/*.py', which would not cover new files. Keep AUDIO_EXTENSIONS a module-level set of dot-prefixed strings, or re-export it: gui-actions-smoke.py regex-scrapes SUPPORTED_EXT from lib.sh and asserts set equality. Natural seams now that the file has grown: the tag/scan bridge, the Track/Album/LibraryIndex model, the CSS token sheet and shared widget helpers (make_cover, track_column_view, track_list_view, StorageMeter), and the window itself.

goals.title: Break up the 4368-line ipod_gui/window.py
goals.description:
The package split left IpodWindow as one module, deliberately: the goal named 'the window itself' as one seam, and splitting a single Adw.ApplicationWindow subclass across files needs mixins, which was too much to combine with the split and its test-harness rewrite in one change.

It is now by far the largest module - 4368 lines against 457 for the next one, player.py - and it holds every view plus the work behind each. Natural seams inside it: the library grid and album detail, the playlist views and their drag reordering, the search field and its two result sections, the Device & Settings page, and the sync/remove/wipe command plumbing with its busy-state bookkeeping.

Mixin classes are the only split that keeps one Adw.ApplicationWindow, so the question to settle first is whether the shared self.* state between those groups is small enough for mixins to be honest rather than a filing system over one namespace. tests/harness.py makes the mechanics safe: it writes a replacement to every module holding a name, so moving methods between modules cannot silently unpatch a check the way it would have before.

Done 2026-08-05. Split into seven mixins over one Adw.ApplicationWindow: library_view, search_view, playlist_view, playback_view, device_view, queue and commands, with window.py keeping the chrome, the state and the assembly order. The largest module is now device_view.py at 929 lines against 4438 before, in line with device.py at 527 and player.py at 457.

The question the goal asked first was settled by measuring rather than by judgement. Counting __init__ makes every attribute look shared, because it is the one place all of them are born; excluding it, 33 of 152 attributes are touched by more than one module, and two thirds of those by exactly two. What is genuinely window-wide is small: the device the window is pointed at, whether a script is running, and the library and the player. So mixins are honest here - but only after the seams were redrawn. The first cut had device and sync sharing twelve attributes, which said they were one concern wearing two names; commands and queue is the cut that works.

Sixteen shared attributes went away rather than being written down, because they were shared only for being built in one module and painted in another. The sidebar's device card, the header's search field and library controls, the playlist rail and the shelf at the top of the library page now belong to whichever mixin repaints them, and the window appends what they return without naming it. Closing the window reached into playback's lock and process handle and now calls one verb; reading the visible view became current_view() for the same reason, since a verb is a declared interface and a widget reached into is not. window.py is left touching exactly one attribute another mixin owns.

device_view.py stayed the largest deliberately. Splitting its page from its probe was measured too, and makes it worse: 33 shared attributes become 36, with 12 shared between the two halves, because painting a device summary and probing the device are one concern.

tools/mixin-contract.py is what keeps this from rotting back. It pins the shared table and checks it in both directions, so a new sharer fails and an entry the code has left behind fails too - adding to it is allowed, doing it by accident is not. It also catches a method defined in two mixins, an attribute read but never assigned, and state assigned but never read. That last check found three dead attributes: now_playing_bar, settings_view and sync_files, all written and never consulted, now gone.

tests/gui-window-build.py builds the real window under xvfb, which nothing did before. Every other GUI check runs methods unbound against a stand-in, deliberately, so none would notice a builder that stopped being called or a widget that never reached the stack - exactly what a mixin split risks. CI gained xvfb for it.

Every one of the 159 methods moved with an identical AST, checked against the pre-split file, so the move could not reword anything; the 11 call sites that did change are the seven extracted builders and the four dead-attribute removals. Both new checks were mutation-tested - removing a builder call, dropping a view from the stack, reaching into another mixin's state, defining a method twice, and mistyping an attribute each fail the check that should catch them. Writing gui-window-build.py surfaced a defect in itself: an exception escaping a GLib idle callback does not end the main loop, so it hung rather than failed, and it now has a watchdog and its own try/except. Full product-e2e.sh passes, 66 checks.

goals.title: Move blocking device work in refresh() off the main loop
goals.description:
count_tracks, list_tracks, list_playlists, spoken_playlists and shutil.disk_usage all run synchronously inside IpodWindow.refresh(), over USB. Tag reading and the library scan are already threaded via scan_tracks with a generation counter to discard stale results; extend the same pattern to the rest. This is the largest remaining responsiveness win and it grows with the number of tracks on the device.

Done 2026-08-04. device.py gained probe_device(), which reads detection, identity, saved options, playlists, spoken names, the track count and free space in one pass and returns a DeviceProbe built complete or not at all. refresh() bumps a probe_generation, hands the read to a worker thread and returns; _apply_probe paints what comes back, and drops a result whose generation was superseded or that landed while a script was changing the device. count_tracks takes the same cancelled callback as scan_tracks, so a superseded walk stops competing for the bus. _populate_device_summary and the wipe dialog read the cached figures rather than the device, so a repaint costs nothing.

list_tracks turned out not to be called from window.py at all, so only the other four moved. Two states came out of it that the old code could not express: a device that stops answering mid-read is now reported as that, rather than as a connected iPod holding nothing, and the first paint says it is looking rather than claiming there is no iPod - which matters because findmnt alone waits five seconds on a device that has stopped answering.

goals.title: Let ipod-sync.sh copy symlinked music
goals.description:
ipod-sync.sh:424 enumerates a source with 'find "$src" -type f -print0'. find does not dereference symlinks by default, so a symlinked audio file is -type l and is silently never copied, and a symlinked subdirectory is never descended. Symlinked library layouts are common, so this is a real long-standing limitation rather than a deliberate policy - it just was not visible before, because nothing counted what was about to be copied.

Verified 2026-08-03: for a directory containing a symlink to an mp3, 'find -type f' returns nothing while Python's os.walk plus Path.is_file() counts the file.

The GUI redesign surfaced this as a mismatch (review-23 in the no-mistakes run merged as PR #11) because it counts queued tracks to drive a progress bar: counting a symlinked track the script then skips means the sync exits successfully with progress short of 100 percent. That was resolved by aligning the GUI DOWNWARD to the script - it now skips symlinks too - so the counts are honest. Making the script actually copy them was the better long-term answer.

Work: switch to 'find -L' (or -follow) in the source enumeration, then add e2e coverage for the cases that makes newly reachable - a symlink loop, a broken symlink, a symlinked directory, and a symlink pointing outside the source tree - and decide whether a symlink escaping the selected folder should be copied at all. Remove the GUI-side symlink skip and its user-facing note at the same time, otherwise the two halves disagree again in the opposite direction.

Done 2026-08-04. ipod-sync.sh enumerates a source with 'find -L "$src" \( -type f -o -type l \) -print0', so a symlinked track is copied and a symlinked folder is descended. A link is followed wherever it points, including out of the folder being synced, because that is what a linked layout is for and the link is only ever read: the copy lands where the link sits inside the source and never where it points, so following one cannot write outside the music directory. That is the opposite of ipod-remove.sh, which resolves before checking containment because it deletes.

Under -L, -type l matches only a link that cannot be resolved, so one walk finds the tracks and the broken links together. A broken link named like a track is reported by path and counted; one named like a cover image stays quiet, because it was never going to be copied. find detects a folder that links back into itself, walks it once and reports it on stderr while exiting 1 - that used to arrive as raw find output in the middle of the copy log, and is now captured and repeated in the script's own voice, which covers an unreadable folder the same way.

The GUI side went the other way, as the goal asked: skip_symlinks, the recursive-no-symlinks reader mode, the per-source skipped counts and the 'symlinked item skipped' toasts and queue-label note are gone, and scan_tracks returns (records, complete). The scan follows links to agree with the script, which needed a loop guard of its own: os.walk has no loop detection and would have recursed forever, so each directory carries its ancestry and one that is its own ancestor is dropped. It deliberately does not dedupe more widely, because two links to one folder are two folders to find, which copies both. tags.walk_following_links holds that rule for _audio_files; the reader cannot call it, being source text run by whichever interpreter has mutagen, so the two are kept deliberately alike.

Fixed along the way: a single dangling *.mp3 link anywhere under a music root made the whole library scan exit 2, so the user saw an empty library because of one broken link. Verified before the change - a folder with good.mp3 next to a dangling link returned no records and complete false.

Covered end to end on its own device, since a source holding a filesystem loop is not something to leave in the shared one: a linked track, a linked folder with a subfolder, a link out of the tree, a dangling audio link, a dangling non-audio link that stays quiet, and a parent loop. tests/gui-scan-paths.py prints what the scan finds so the suite can hold it against what the sync copied, which is the mismatch this goal existed to close. Mutation-checked: reverting to 'find -type f' aborts the suite exactly at that scenario, copying 1 of 4 tracks.

goals.title: wipe the ipod and redownload everything
Make it easier to create a new playlist
goals.description:
Currently, in order to create a new playlist, you need to choose a playlist file.

Instead, creating a playlist should be low friction like spotify where it creates everything for you, and you just get the option to name the new playlist (start with default name like Playlist #_ if none is typed). 

Then it should be easy to add songs to the playlist from yt-dlp or from the existing library. It should also be easy to move songs between playlists and remove back to the standard library.

If you have any other suggestions let me know, i'm open to anything.

Done 2026-08-05. A playlist is now a file the app writes rather than one you had to bring with you: one M3U per list under ~/Music/Playlists, which ipod_gui/playlists.py owns. Making one is a name and nothing else - the new dialog offers the next free 'Playlist N', refuses a name FAT cannot hold while it is being typed rather than letting ipod-sync.sh mangle it into a different spoken name two steps later, and writes the file when it closes. No iPod, no export from another program, no sync to wait for.

Songs go in from a ⋯ menu on every track row - the library table, an album page, and both halves of the search results - plus an album-level Add to playlist. A YouTube result carries the same menu: it downloads first and lands in the playlist when it finishes, found by video id rather than by what the run reported, because a video the music folder already holds downloads nothing and reports nothing. A previewed track is kept into the library before it is listed, since an entry pointing into a cache that gets pruned would stop resolving with nothing having been deleted on purpose. Inside a playlist the same menu moves a track to another playlist or removes it, which is what the goal asked for and leaves the song itself alone.

Every edit rewrites the file and stages the playlist and its tracks for the next sync; an emptied one is still staged, because the sync is what removes the device's copy. Editing with no iPod attached is not a failure - Send to iPod stages it when one turns up. Without a speech engine the playlist stays here and the page says why, which is the old refusal moved from making a playlist to putting one on a screenless device.

Device playlists are still listed beside them - a folder or tag grouping, or a list made elsewhere - but read-only, because their entries name scrambled files on the iPod with no local counterpart to write down. The rail and shelf now carry the same state dot a track does, since the spoken-name marker they used to show says nothing about a playlist that has never been synced, and every new one starts out as exactly that. Add playlist file… became Import playlist file…, which adopts the list into the folder with its entries resolved instead of pointing at where it sat.

Two defects were caught by measuring rather than by looking. A row of four action buttons took the narrowest the window could be from 640px to 730px, past the point where the sidebar has already folded away to make room; it is two buttons and a ⋯ now, and the Playlists view is narrower than before this goal at 426→574px against 545px. And a ⋯ at row opacity beside two solid buttons reads as disabled, so the one a page carries alone is full strength.

Covered by tests/gui-playlists.py, which asserts the file after every edit and what each one staged, and by two end-to-end steps that take a list built by that same store through ipod-sync.sh: the order a track was dragged into survives onto the device, and emptying a playlist removes it from the device while keeping its songs. Eleven mutations checked, each caught by the check that should: de-duplication, staging, re-staging the source of a move, deleting the file, removing the old device playlist after a rename, the emptied-playlist rule, refusing a device-only track, the row menu, selecting a new playlist, painting the detail, and queueing the list itself alongside its tracks. Full product-e2e.sh passes, 69 checks.

goals.title: Add top bar to maximize/minimize/close the window
Get the grouping drop-down working again on a 2x display
goals.description:
DONE 2026-08-07. Not this app's code and not a GTK bug: mutter refused to place the popup and dismissed it. The refusal is in the journal, 491 times in one boot, bursty and clustered on exactly the sessions where the drop-down was being clicked: 'Buggy client caused popup to be placed outside of parent window'. That message has one source in mutter 46, the rect check closing meta_wayland_xdg_popup_post_apply_state, which calls dismiss_invalid_popup and so sends xdg_popup.popup_done when the popup's buffer rect neither overlaps nor touches its parent's. The check runs on the commit that attaches the popup's first buffer, which is the popup_done arriving about 10ms after the map. It also explains the one asymmetry nothing else did: maximised, the parent covers the screen and a mis-placed popup still lands on it; floating, the parent is a small target and the popup misses.

The mis-placement came from the session's layout mode rather than from the widget. DisplayConfig reported layout-mode 2 (physical) with legacy-ui-scaling-factor 2, so mutter was on the legacy HiDPI path, where scale_placement_rule multiplies every positioner coordinate by the window's monitor scale. get_window_geometry_scale_for_logical_monitor returns 1 instead when meta_backend_is_stage_views_scaled is true, which is exactly when scale-monitor-framebuffer is on.

FIXED by turning on Fractional Scaling for the built-in display in Settings, which sets org.gnome.mutter experimental-features to ['scale-monitor-framebuffer'] and moves the session to layout-mode 1 with legacy-ui-scaling-factor 1. The last refusal was logged at 05:04, the display configuration was applied at 05:06:58, and there have been none since. No code changed and the Gtk.DropDown stays. To re-check at any time: journalctl --user -b | grep -c 'outside of parent window' should stay flat while clicking the control.

COST ACCEPTED, and it does not depend on the external monitor being attached: with stage views scaled, mutter hardcodes the UI scaling factor for X11 clients to 1 (meta-settings.c, update_ui_scaling_factor). Measured, X11 clients are told eDP-1 is 1536x960 at scale 1 with Xft.dpi 96, so XWayland apps draw at 1x and are upscaled on the 2x panel where the legacy path had them drawing at 2x; Wayland clients are told scale 2 and stay sharp. GNOME 46 has no xwayland-native-scaling to avoid that. Both displays are on integer scales, 2.0 and 1.0, so nothing is resampled and the power, speed and sharpness warnings on the Settings toggle do not apply to this configuration. The setting is session-wide and stays on undocked, which is what is wanted, because this is a floating-on-a-2x-display bug rather than a two-monitor one and the laptop alone is still 2x.

CORRECTS the earlier reading of the WAYLAND_DEBUG trace: the reactive positioner and the mid-map wp_fractional_scale change are upstream of the mis-placement, not the dismissal itself. The routes listed before are moot - GTK did not need updating past 4.14.5, the Gtk.MenuButton replacement was not needed, and the layered minimal.py reproduction is not needed to verify this.

goals.title: Let the search box own pasted YouTube links
goals.description:
Pasting a YouTube link into the search field already works and almost nobody would know: youtube_search_target (ipod_gui/youtube.py:83) detects a link and looks it up as itself rather than searching for the text as a phrase. Two gaps keep it from being the real home for the feature.

It is undiscoverable. The search entry's placeholder is "Search your library and YouTube" (search_view.py:52) and never mentions links, which is why the Add from YouTube dialog on the Device page still gets reached for.

A pasted playlist link is silently truncated. youtube_search_command caps every query with --playlist-items 1-<limit> (youtube.py:103) and YOUTUBE_SEARCH_RESULTS is 3 (youtube.py:36), so pasting a 40 track playlist shows three results and reads as the whole thing. The cap is right for keeping an album link from flooding the section, but presenting the first three as if they were all of it is wrong on its own terms, separate from anything to do with the dialog.

The work: say so in the placeholder, and when the query resolves to a playlist show a header above the YouTube section naming it and its real length, along the lines of "Playlist: Name, 40 tracks, showing first 3", with an Add all action beside it. That puts the whole playlist download at the moment it is relevant instead of behind a switch on a settings page, and it fixes the truncation at the same time. parse_search_results (youtube.py:110) currently drops the playlist_title, playlist_count and n_entries that --flat-playlist --dump-json emits for a playlist URL, and SearchResult (youtube.py:53) has no field to carry them, so both need to keep that metadata for the header to exist.

Add all needs no new download path: _start_youtube_download(url, single=False) is exactly what the dialog's Whole playlist switch did (queue.py:676).

Carry over the clipboard convenience too. _offer_clipboard_url (queue.py:663) pre-filled the dialog from the clipboard and is removed along with it, so when the search field is empty and the clipboard holds a downloadable URL, offer it as a suggestion. Offer rather than autofill, so a clipboard that happens to hold a link never silently changes what a search is about to run.

Rationale for not simply moving the dialog somewhere else: a dedicated entry point made sense when search could not resolve links, and it can. A second one duplicates a working path and puts the capability on a settings page rather than the page actually in use.

This must land before "Drop the Sync options card and the three add buttons from Device and settings", because it is what keeps whole playlist downloading alive once that dialog goes.

Done 2026-08-08. The placeholder reads "Search or paste a link", with the sentence naming both sources moved to the field's tooltip: it does not fit in a 26-character field, and a placeholder is clipped rather than ellipsised. The tooltip is also what a screen reader reads out, since the field carries no label.

A pasted link that resolves to a list now gets a header above the rows - "Playlist: Name, 15 tracks, showing the first 3" - with Add all beside it, which is _start_youtube_download(url, single=False), the dialog's Whole playlist switch by another name. Add all joins search_add_buttons, so a device appearing or a script starting reaches it like any row's Add.

SearchResult carries playlist_title and playlist_count. n_entries is deliberately not carried: measured against real yt-dlp output, playlist_count is the whole list while n_entries is what --playlist-items left, so reading n_entries would report the truncation as the length, which is the bug. The other finding from that output decides the design: ytsearchN: is a playlist to yt-dlp too, and every entry of a plain search comes back with playlist_title set to the query, so linked_playlist() refuses to answer unless the query is a link. Without that gate every search would announce itself as a playlist named after what was typed.

A link carrying a playlist - the watch?v=...&list=... form the address bar gives you mid-playlist - resolves to the playlist rather than to the single video, so the header names it and Add all takes the whole thing. The three rows are the playlist's first three, which need not include the video the link was of. Measured rather than assumed: an earlier draft of this note and of the README both claimed the opposite, from reasoning about yt-dlp instead of running it, and the review caught it. Case 4 of 06-what-yt-dlp-reports.txt is that measurement.

Add all is offered only for a list yt-dlp gave a length for. A Mix, a channel and an @handle report none, because they are paginated rather than finite, so the header names the list and stops there and each row keeps its own Add: a one-press fetch of a listing with no stated end onto a player with two gigabytes on it is not something to offer. Case 5 of 06-what-yt-dlp-reports.txt is that measurement.

The clipboard convenience is a strip under the header rather than a popover over the field, because a popover is placed by the compositor and this window's one drop-down is already dismissed on sight under GNOME's legacy HiDPI scaling. It appears when the empty field is focused, offers the link rather than typing it in, and offers each link once so a turned-down suggestion does not come back on every visit.

Verified against real YouTube in the Xephyr recipe from tools/demo-library.py, with xdotool clicks and a real X clipboard: Add all was read off the process table, not the log pane, and fetched all fifteen streams of a fifteen-track playlist. Evidence in .no-mistakes/evidence/search-owns-pasted-links. Ten mutations of the new checks were each caught. tests/gui-window-minimum.py now reveals the strip and paints the header before measuring, since a hidden child measures as nothing and neither would ever have been checked against the window's minimum.

goals.title: Answer a deleted playlist apart from one that could not be read
goals.description:
playlist_contents catches every OSError alike, so a playlist another program deleted while its rows are on screen answers complete=False and the window says it could not write - sending the user to check permissions on a folder that is perfectly writable, while the rail keeps showing a playlist that is gone. Making playlist_contents answer FileNotFoundError apart from a genuine read failure closes it for add_entries, remove_entry and move_entry at once, rather than at each of the three edit sites. A deleted playlist should repaint, the way a vanished row already does; a real read failure should keep saying so. Raised by review on playlist-edit-failure-wording, which fixed the shortened-file half of the same symptom. Deliberate and module-wide today: tests/gui-playlists.py asserts the current answer for add_entries on a deleted file, so those assertions move with the change.

Done 2026-08-08. Told apart in playlist_contents, which closes it for add_entries, remove_entry and move_entry at once: every edit here begins by reading the list it is about to rewrite, so that read is the one place the missing file is met. The three of them answer PLAYLIST_GONE, a second falsy sentinel beside TARGET_GONE - both are now one _Gone class with two named singletons, and identity is what keeps a playlist that has gone from being read as the row it was dropped on having gone.

The error is not what tells them apart, which is the trap the naive fix falls into. A playlist symlinked onto a drive that is not plugged in raises FileNotFoundError exactly as a deleted one does, and it is still sitting in the folder - so the directory entry is asked instead, with lstat rather than a read. Only a definite nothing-is-at-that-path answers PLAYLIST_GONE: a folder that cannot be stat'ed leaves it unanswered, and unanswered keeps the old answer, because taking a playlist off the rail claims more than saying it could not be read does.

The window repaints and names the playlist for every edit that meets one: adding, removing, reordering, either end of a move, and a download landing in a playlist. A move whose source has gone is not a failure at all - the track arrived where it was going and there is nothing left to take it out of - so it reports the move and says the source has gone. The move's target mattered more than a wrong sentence: PLAYLIST_GONE is not None, so without the check the old test fell through and removed the track from the source it had never landed beside. Three stale-cache siblings were answered the same way while they were open, being the same thing found one step earlier from the window's own list: removing a track was silent, and the move and the YouTube add left the vanished playlist on the rail.

Reproduced before the fix and verified after it against the real window under a display, with real widgets and no stand-in: the rail loses the row and the toast reads There is no playlist called Road Trip, where the same script got Could not read Road Trip and a rail that still held it. Every new check was mutation-tested, including the FileNotFoundError-alone fix, which fails on the unplugged drive, and the dropped target check, which silently empties the source playlist. The assertions tests/gui-playlists.py made about the old answer moved with the change. Full product-e2e.sh passes, 69 checks.

goals.title: Library page: playlist covers, a Queued marker, and Delete from library
goals.description:
Three merged UI goals, all on the library page and on the track rows it shares with the album, search and playlist pages.

Covers on playlists: a tile on the library shelf and a row in either playlist rail both draw make_cover(None, ...), so every playlist is a generated placeholder even when every song it lists carries artwork. Take the first cover any of its tracks has, for a device playlist as well as one made here, and fall back to the placeholder only when nothing in it has art. The playlist detail page keeps no cover: it already measures 625px against the 640px minimum the window advertises, and tests/gui-window-minimum.py is what says so.

Queued filter and symbol: the library's state pills are All / On iPod / In library / Previewed, and a track staged for the next sync looks exactly like one that is not, apart from the word on its own Add button. Add a fourth state, queued, decided in _merge_states beside the other three so that every dot, label, pill and count derives from it rather than from a second rule. An album is Queued when all of it is either on the iPod or staged, which is the rule On iPod already follows.

Delete from library: nothing in the window can delete a song. Put it in the menu a track row already carries, for tracks on this computer only - never a device-only entry, never a preview - behind a confirmation that says what happens to the copy on the iPod and to the playlists that list it. The file goes to the wastebasket rather than being unlinked, and the track is dropped from the queue and from the library index.

goals.title: Drop the Sync options card and the three add buttons from Device and settings
goals.description:
Everything under Sync options on the Device and settings page is now reachable elsewhere in the GUI, so the card and the three action buttons beside it go.

Remove the Playlist grouping ComboRow and the Speak track names / Speak playlist names switches from _build_sync_options (ipod_gui/device_view.py:203). Syncing should always use no automatic grouping with both spoken names on, so _sync_options (device_view.py:884) returns ["--voiceover", "--playlist-voiceover"], falling back to ["--forget-options"] when has_speech_engine() is false, because spoken names cannot be generated without an engine. Keep the warning card that explains a missing engine. Passing explicit flags is also what clears stale state rather than needing a migration: ipod-sync.sh replays a device's saved .sync-options only when DB_ARGS is empty (ipod-sync.sh:130), so a device that already has --auto-dir-playlists written into iPod_Control/.sync-options stops grouping on its next sync.

Remove the three buttons at device_view.py:287-309 (Add music folder..., Import playlist file..., Add from YouTube...) along with the dialog plumbing only they reach: on_add_music (queue.py:551), on_import_playlist (playlist_view.py:1099), on_add_youtube (queue.py:622), _on_youtube_response and _offer_clipboard_url. Keep _discover_music_folder, _import_playlist and _start_youtube_download. Those take a path or a URL directly instead of opening a chooser, they are where the actual work lives, and they are the seam the headless CLI and Gio actions goals under Agent interfaces would drive. _start_youtube_download already has three other callers, and _import_playlist is a thin wrapper over import_playlist_file (playlists.py:274), which stays regardless.

The home page already covers what the buttons did. youtube_search_target (youtube.py:83) detects a pasted link and looks it up as itself rather than searching for the text as a phrase, so a URL pasted into search resolves to that video. Folders are added under Music folders and their tracks queued from the Library. Playlists are made with the New button. The Whole playlist toggle is the one thing search does not yet cover, which is why "Let the search box own pasted YouTube links" is a prerequisite rather than this goal accepting the loss: that goal moves whole playlist downloading into the search results, and this one must not land first.

Also update the button list in window.py:187-189, the sensitivity rules in _update_device_controls (device_view.py:626-633), _load_sync_options (device_view.py:871) and its probe call at device_view.py:460, and saved_sync_options (device.py:105, called at device.py:485), which decodes the grouping mode out of .sync-options and would be left with no reader. Tests that touch this surface: tests/gui-window-build.py, tests/gui-state-smoke.py, tests/gui-actions-smoke.py, tests/gui-playlists.py.

Worth landing before "A headless CLI over the ipod_gui package" so the CLI does not wrap controls that are about to disappear.

Done 2026-08-11, with two deviations from the spec above.

_sync_options returns ["--voiceover", "--playlist-voiceover"] unconditionally; the --forget-options fallback specified above was rejected during review. --forget-options makes ipod-sync.sh delete iPod_Control/.sync-options, and the device-playlist drag reorder runs a rebuild with no speech gate at all, so one drag on a machine with no engine erased the saved state and every later replay-based rebuild ran bare - including the one ipod-remove.sh does for the GUI's own per-track Remove. Passing the flags still retires a stale --auto-dir-playlists, which was the actual requirement, because ipod-sync.sh overwrites that file with whatever it is given.

Related and worth knowing before touching this: the builder empties iPod_Control/Speakable/Tracks and Speakable/Playlists at the start of every run and only refills what it can speak, so any sync or rebuild from a machine with no engine leaves the whole device unnamed. That predates this goal and is not fixed by it. What the flags buy is the way back, since they are saved to the device and the next rebuild from a machine that can speak records every name again. The Device & Settings warning card and the three confirmation dialogs that rebuild - remove track, delete device playlist, rename device playlist - now say so.

Adopting a foreign playlist file left the GUI rather than moving: on_import_playlist is gone and _import_playlist has no caller but the tests. A .pls and a relative-path .m3u have no route in at all until the headless CLI and Gio actions goals land, which the README now states plainly. That was accepted deliberately.

Split out of the review: "Refuse a device playlist rename that cannot restage the new name".

goals.title: JSON output and stable exit codes for the shell scripts
goals.description: The read-only surface first. ipod-remove.sh --list is the only report of what is on the device and it prints prose; nothing in the repository emits machine-readable output at all, and the only --json in the tree is the GUI consuming findmnt's in lib.sh and device.py. Add --json to the paths that report rather than act, covering the mount point, device identity, free space, track count, track paths, playlists, spoken names and the saved sync options - which is the same set probe_device() already assembles for the window. Give the states a caller has to branch on distinct exit codes rather than English: no iPod, several iPods, the device stopped answering mid-operation, a missing dependency, and a declined prompt. install.sh's capability probes should be able to report the same way, so a caller can find out what is installed without running an install. The standard to meet is already in the tree: ipod-fetch.sh --new-tracks FILE deletes the file rather than leaving it stale when yt-dlp cannot fill it, because a stale file reads as a definite answer to whoever picks it up next. Every JSON path here owes the same guarantee - a definite answer or no answer, never a stale one.

goals.title: Structured sync progress, replacing the GUI's regex scrape
goals.description: text.py holds COPIED_LINE, a regex that parses '+ name -> dest' out of ipod-sync.sh's coloured human output, and that scrape is what drives the sync bar; strip_ansi sits beside it because the escape sequences otherwise arrived in the log view as literal noise. Rewording one line of the script silently breaks the progress bar, and nothing fails when it does. Emit one JSON object per line on a separate stream, either fd 3 or behind --progress-json, covering the planned total, each file copied, the database rebuild starting and finishing, playlist writes, and the terminal result. Then have commands.py consume that instead of the regex. The human output stays exactly as it is: this is an additional stream, not a replacement, because the scripts are the product and they have to keep reading well in a terminal. The same protocol should cover ipod-remove.sh and ipod-wipe.sh, since commands.py runs all three through one _run and shows them in the same bar.

goals.title: Rails for destructive operations run non-interactively
goals.description: This has to land with the first machine interface rather than after it, because the first JSON path into ipod-wipe.sh is also the first way an agent wipes someone's iPod by accident. Three parts. A --dry-run on sync, remove and wipe that prints the exact plan as JSON and touches nothing. An --expect-device <identity> that promotes the check commands.py already makes into something a caller can demand: every device-changing action there holds the write side of DEVICE_IO_LOCK and re-resolves the mount to confirm the iPod under it is still the one the action was aimed at, and that guarantee currently stops at the GUI's edge. And a refusal to run a destructive action non-interactively without an explicit token, even when --yes is passed, since --yes today means a human already decided and a caller passing it programmatically means nothing of the kind. The suite already covers a track path escaping the music folder through ../ on the way into an rm -rf, and a wipe destroying Apple's Speakable prompts, which nothing in the open-source toolchain can regenerate. These rails belong under the same coverage, and the e2e suite is where they get it.

goals.title: A headless CLI over the ipod_gui package
goals.description: Everything worth asking the app lives in ipod_gui/ and is reachable only by building a GTK window, even though most of those modules never touch a widget. Expose them as python3 -m ipod_gui.cli with subcommands: library for the LibraryIndex (tracks, albums, artists, counts and each track's state), device for one probe_device() pass, search for local_search_matches plus search_youtube, playlists for the M3U folder (list, create, add, remove, reorder), cache for the preview cache (size, prune, clear), and config for the music roots and layout. The logic already exists and is display-free; the work is the command surface and the output shape, which follows the conventions the shell scripts get. One constraint to respect: ipod_gui/__init__.py imports gi and pins Gtk 4.0 and Adw 1 eagerly, and tests/harness.py depends on that declared ordering to know which binding a stand-in has to replace, so the CLI enters through the package rather than around it and must not become a second import path the harness cannot reach. It needs PyGObject installed but no display. Extend the CI Python gate, which today only compiles the package and tests/*.py.

goals.title: Gio actions and a state dump on the running window
goals.description: The app already owns a D-Bus name and exports nothing on it: IpodApp is an Adw.Application constructed with APP_ID and DEFAULT_FLAGS, and GtkApplication publishes org.gtk.Actions on that name for free. Adding actions makes a running window drivable by gdbus call, with no synthetic input events and no AT-SPI. Add navigate(page), search(query), queue(path) and refresh, and a dump-state that returns JSON of what is actually on screen: the current page, the visible counts, what is staged for the next sync, the now-playing state, the sync bar's state, and any inline error a view is showing in place of content - which the search design in particular requires be stated inline rather than as a toast, so it is only visible in the widget tree. That last field is what lets a check assert on the app's state instead of interpreting a screenshot. DEFAULT_FLAGS makes the app single-instance, so a second launch activates the existing window rather than opening a second one: that is the hook this depends on, not a problem to work around. Serialise the library and device objects with the same code the headless CLI uses, so there is one shape for them rather than two that drift.

goals.title: A deterministic screenshot harness for the window
goals.description: Verifying this window visually has been hand-rolled every time it was needed, and the reason is already recorded in the search UI polish goal: x11grab sees black under Wayland and a WidgetPaintable holds nothing when the compositor is not sending window frames, so the approach that worked was forcing the layout with Gtk.Widget.allocate and snapshotting into a Cairo renderer, which makes the size a parameter of the shot rather than whatever the window manager happened to give. Promote that into tools/shoot.py, taking a page, a width, a scale factor and an output path, driven through the navigate action rather than by reaching into the widget tree. Run it against the fixture tools/demo-library.py builds, so the shots are deterministic and show the same four albums and two playlists every time. The scale factor is not optional: the most recent fix in this repository was a grouping drop-down that only misbehaved on a 2x display, and no 1x shot would have shown it. Consider running a small set of shots in CI and keeping them as artifacts, beside the two real-window checks that already run under xvfb.

goals.title: An MCP server over the headless CLI
goals.description: So the app is reachable from a client that is not sitting in this checkout with a shell. A thin server over the headless CLI's subcommands, adding no logic of its own: library, device, search, playlists and cache as read-only tools, and the device-changing ones only behind the rails, which means every destructive tool takes the expected device identity and offers the dry run first. Keep the two sets visibly separate in the tool listing rather than relying on a description to carry the difference, since the failure mode here is a caller that cannot see the boundary reaching across it. Ship it under tools/ and document it in the README. This is the last piece and the most optional: it is worth doing only once the CLI beneath it is the real interface rather than a wrapper around scraped output.

goals.title: A repo skill and CLAUDE.md so an agent starts from the right facts
goals.description: There is no .claude/ in this repository and no repo-level CLAUDE.md, so the entry point for anyone arriving without context is a 54,000 character README. Write the short version of what has to be known before touching anything: that the shell scripts are the product and the GUI drives them rather than reimplementing their device-changing logic; which actions are destructive and what the rails around them require; the mixin boundary and that tools/mixin-contract.py checks it; the import ordering ipod_gui/__init__.py declares and tests/harness.py depends on; how to run the suite, including xvfb for the two real-window checks, IPOD_REAL_DB_TOOL for the upstream database builder and EVIDENCE_DIR for the artefacts; and the demo library recipe. Then document the machine interfaces the other goals in this group add, so they are found rather than rediscovered. It lands after them for that reason.

goals.title: Count queued tracks the library index does not hold
goals.description:
The library page's Queued pill can read 0 while the sidebar reads '+120 MB queued to sync' and the Sync button reads 'Sync 30 changes'.

_populate_albums counts from LibraryIndex.counts()/track_counts(), which walk all_tracks() = tracks + device_only + previews. A folder staged through the header's 'Add music folder…' button (on_add_music -> _discover_music_folder -> _finish_music_folder_discovery in queue.py) is queued without being added to library.roots - that is on_add_folder in device_view.py, a different button - so its tracks land in _pending_track_index only and never reach library.tracks.

The gap is older than the pill: those tracks are already absent from the grid and from every other pill. Naming a count is what made it visible, and it was deliberately left out of the goal that added the pill. Decide whether a queued track no music folder holds belongs in the album grid at all - if it does, the merge is where it would join, and the pill and its filter then agree with the Sync button by construction.

Done 2026-08-09. A queued track no music folder holds does belong in the grid, and the merge is where it joins: LibraryIndex gained a fourth list, queued_only, filled by the same pass of _merge_states that already built the queue's accounting index. The pill, its filter and the Sync button now count one thing by construction rather than by agreement.

Reproduced end to end first, against the real window with a folder of tagged MP3s outside every music root: the sidebar read '+60 KB queued to sync' and the button 'Sync 3 changes' while every pill above the grid read zero of them, and those tracks were in no view in the app at all.

Two things fell out of making them visible. A staged track the iPod already holds was matched against the device's copy without claiming it, which was harmless while nothing drew these tracks and would now put the same song in the grid twice - once as the file waiting here, once as the copy over there; the pending loop claims it the way the library loop does. And _clear_pending rebuilt the accounting index by hand, which would leave the grid calling tracks queued for a sync that had just copied them, so it calls _merge_states instead - one rule in one place rather than a copy that goes stale.

The check lives in tests/gui-window-build.py, the only one that builds the real window, and reads the two counts against each other rather than each alone: what the Sync button offers to copy and what the Queued pill says is staged are the same tracks, and checking either on its own is what let them disagree. Mutation-tested - dropping the list from all_tracks, leaving the device copy unclaimed, and restoring the hand-written reset each fail the assertion meant to catch them.

Writing it surfaced a gap next door: the library loop's own claim was covered by nothing, so deleting it - which would put every synced song in the grid twice - passed the whole suite. gui-actions-smoke now asserts device_only is empty in the matched case, as it already did in the unmatched one.

Read in the app against the demo library with a folder staged from outside it: the grid reads All 5 / On iPod 1 / Queued 1 / In library 3, the fifth card wearing the Queued badge and its own artwork; the table reads Queued 4 and filters to the four staged rows, each offering Unqueue; the sidebar reads +80.1 KB queued to sync. Full product-e2e.sh passes, 69 checks.

goals.title: Images in songs + playlists
goals.description: Are the images in the playlists and songs getting added to the shuffle? Shouldn't all the covers be local to the computer? Also can we add an option to add custom playlist covers.

goals.title: Refuse a device playlist rename that cannot restage the new name
goals.description:
Renaming a playlist that is already on the iPod takes it off the device and cannot always put it back.

_on_rename_response (ipod_gui/playlist_view.py) renames the local file, calls _stage_playlist(new_name), and then calls _remove_device_playlist(old_name) regardless of whether the staging succeeded. _stage_playlists returns early with the not-queued note when playlist_unavailable is set, so on a machine with no speech engine nothing is staged - and the removal still runs, so ipod-remove.sh strips the playlist off the device. Send to iPod cannot restage it either, because _can_send_playlist also requires speech_engine_available. The playlist leaves the iPod and stays gone until an engine is installed and the user notices they have to re-send it.

It is not a one-line guard, because nothing _stage_playlists hands back says whether staging was possible: it returns "" for non-failure cases as well, so an empty note does not mean "did not stage". Renaming an empty playlist the device holds is the case that breaks the obvious reading. It takes the not-entries-and-not-on-device branch, since the new name is not on the device yet, so nothing is wanted and the call returns "" - while _playlist_on_device(old_name) is still true and the removal is exactly what should run. Skip it there and the old name stays on the iPod as a device-only playlist: its row's Delete still reaches it, but no automatic path takes it off any more, because that name is never staged again. Finding a signal that separates "could not stage" from "nothing to stage" is the actual work, wherever that signal ends up living.

Split out of "Drop the Sync options card and the three add buttons from Device and settings", which corrected the dialog's wording so it stops promising a sync that cannot happen.

Done 2026-08-11. Refused rather than made conditional: the rename that cannot restage the new name never starts, so nothing is renamed here either. The alternative - rename locally and leave the device copy - trades one stranding for another, since the window would then show the new name beside a device-only playlist under the old one, with no automatic path taking either off.

The signal is _staging_wanted(playlist, on_device=None), factored out of _stage_playlists' own not-entries-and-not-on-device branch so the two cannot drift. The rename asks it with on_device=False, which is the whole trick: the staging happens after the file moves, under a name the device does not hold, and it never can - the dialog refuses every name the page already shows and the device's own playlists are shown. Under that name the question collapses to whether the playlist lists anything, which is exactly what separates 'could not stage' from 'nothing to stage'.

_rename_refusal returns the sentence to say rather than a flag, so what is refused and the way out of it are one decision. Asked twice: before the dialog opens, and again before the file moves, because a probe can put the playlist on the device while the dialog stands open.

The empty playlist the device holds still has its old name removed, which is the case the obvious guard breaks. Nothing is staged for it under either name and nothing needs to be, so the note _stage_playlists returns is the same "" a refusal leaves - while the removal there is the only thing that will ever take that list off the iPod.

Two wording defects fell out of the same predicate. The confirmation had promised 'stages the new name for the next sync' for an empty playlist on the device, which stages nothing whatever the engine; it now says so. And the no-engine branch's 'the playlist leaves the iPod and does not come back' described a loss the app no longer allows - the only rename that still reaches that dialog is the empty one, where the removal is correct - so it is gone, with SPOKEN_NAMES_LOST left where every other rebuilding confirmation carries it.

Reproduced end to end first, driving the real _on_rename_response against a fake iPod and letting the removal actually run ipod-remove.sh: the playlist file left the volume root with nothing queued to put it back. The same driver confirms the fix and the empty-playlist case. Both are permanent checks now, in gui-playlists.py for what a press does and says and in gui-window-build.py for which dialog the real window presents; five mutations were each caught by at least one of them. gui-window-build.py also gained a helper moving speech_engine_available and playlist_unavailable together, since __init__ derives both from one probe and flipping only the flag was passing a check against behaviour no user gets. Full product-e2e.sh passes, 70 checks.
